title: The impact of tumor vessel infiltration on long-term outcomes in solid malignancies – a prospective multicenter international observational trial
summary: Cancer can grow into nearby blood vessels during the course of the disease. This process may facilitate tumor progression, complicate treatment decisions, and negatively affect patient survival. However, little is known about how frequently blood vessel infiltration occurs across different types of solid cancers, which factors contribute to its development, and how it influences long-term outcomes. The aim of this study is to follow patients with solid tumors over several years and analyze routinely collected clinical information, medical imaging data, and blood and tissue samples. By combining these data sources, the study seeks to improve the understanding of the biological mechanisms and risk factors associated with tumor vessel infiltration and to identify markers that may help predict disease progression. The findings may contribute to improved diagnosis, prognosis assessment, and future treatment strategies for cancer patients. No additional treatments or procedures beyond routine clinical care are required for participation in this study.
conditions: Solid malignancies: colorectal cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, esophageal cancer, adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction (AEG), gastric cancer, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), cholangiocarcinoma, sarcomas, breast cancer, cervical cancer, ovarian cancer, lung cancer, prostate cancer, renal cell carcinoma, melanoma, and head and neck malignancies.

interventions.name:
Patients with solid malignancies are enrolled after written informed consent in this prospective multicenter observational study. At baseline, clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, radiological imaging, and available tumor tissue and blood samples are collected.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a solid malignancy
Written informed consent for study participation
Age ≥ 18 years (oder: 18 years of age or older)
Exclusion criteria:
Second primary malignancy diagnosed within the previous 5 years (excluding basal cell carcinoma, cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, carcinoma in situ, intraepithelial neoplasia, and thyroid microcarcinoma)
Absence of written informed consent
Carcinoma of unknown primary (CUP)
Primary central nervous system malignancy
